questions.q: If a copper wire is stretched to& increase its length by& $20 %$. The percentage increase in resistance of the wire is _____%.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Before heating, resistance of wire is& ${R}_{0} = \left(\dfrac{ρ{l}_{0}}{A0}\right)

After heating, resistance is~$R = $\dfrac{ρl}{A}

As volume = constant

Therefore,

${A}_{0}{l}_{0} = 1 . 2{l}_{0}A$

$⇒ A = \left(\dfrac{A0}{1 . 2}\right)$

So,

$R = \dfrac{ρl}{A} = ρ \times \left(1 . 2{l}_{0}\right)\left(\dfrac{A0}{1 . 2}\right) = \dfrac{ρ{l}_{0}}{A0} \times 1 . 44 = 1 . 44{R}_{0}$

Percentage increase in~$R$~$= \dfrac{R - {R}_{0}}{R0} \times 100 = 44 %$

$

questions.q: All resistances in figure are $1Ω$ each. The value of current '$I$' is $\dfrac{a}{5}A$. The value of $a$& is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Each pair on the right side of the circuit is in parallel connection, hence it can be replaced by a resistance of& $\dfrac{r}{2}$~as shown.

Now,~$r \text{ and } \dfrac{r}{2}$~in each branch on the right side is in series, hence combined resistance value will be,~$\dfrac{3r}{2}$. Upper branch having resistance~$\dfrac{3r}{2}$~is in parallel with another~$\dfrac{3r}{2}$, hence it can be written as~$\dfrac{3r}{4}$.

Further, simplified circuit will have net resistance of~$\dfrac{7r}{8}$.

Therefore,~${R}_{eq} = \dfrac{7r}{8} + r = \dfrac{7}{8} + 1 = \dfrac{15}{8}Ω$

Now, current~$I = \dfrac{3}{\dfrac{15}{8}} = \dfrac{8}{5}A$

Hence, value of~$a = 8$.

The value of $x$, to the nearest integer, is

questions.q: Two cells are connected in opposition as shown. Cell ${E}_{1}$ is of $8V$ emf and $2Ω$ internal resistance; the cell ${E}_{2}$ is of $2V$ emf and $4Ω$ internal resistance. The terminal potential difference of cell ${E}_{2}$ is ______ $V$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Current in circuit, $I = \dfrac{8 - 2}{2 + 4} = \dfrac{6}{6} = 1A$

Applying Kirchhoff's law from $C$ to $B$,

${V}_{C} - 2 - 4 \times 1 = {V}_{B}$

$⇒ {V}_{C} - {V}_{B} = 6V$

questions.q:
Seawater at a frequency $f = 9 \times {10}^{2}Hz$, has permittivity $ε = 80{ε}_{0}$ and resistivity $ρ = 0 . 25Ωm$. Imagine a parallel plate capacitor is immersed in seawater and is driven by an alternating voltage source $V ( t ) = {V}_{0}sin ( 2\pift )$. Then the conduction current density becomes ${10}^{x}$ times the displacement current density after time $t = \dfrac{1}{800}s .$ The value of $x$ is _______

(Given \left: \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}} = 9 \times {10}^{9}Nm^{2}C^{- 2}\right)$

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${J}_{c} = \dfrac{E}{ρ} = \dfrac{V}{ρd}$

${J}_{d} = \dfrac{1}{A}\dfrac{dq}{dt}= \dfrac{C}{A}\dfrac{d{V}_{c}}{dt}= \dfrac{ϵ}{d}\dfrac{d{V}_{c}}{dt}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{V}_{0}sin2\pift}{ρd} = {10}^{x} \times \dfrac{80{ε}_{0}}{d}{V}_{0} ( 2\pif ) cos2\pift$

$tan\left(2\pi \times \dfrac{900}{800}\right) = {10}^{x} \times \dfrac{40}{9 \times {10}^{9}} \times 900$

$= x = 6$

questions.q: In the given figure, the value of ${V}_{0}$ will be _____~$V$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using Kirchhoff's junction rule,

$\dfrac{{V}_{0} - 2}{1kΩ} + \dfrac{{V}_{0} - 4}{1kΩ} + \dfrac{{V}_{0} - 6}{1kΩ} = 0$

$3{V}_{0} - 12 = 0$

${V}_{0} = 4V$

questions.q: A potential& ${V}_{0}$~is applied across a uniform wire of resistance~$R .$ The power dissipation is~${P}_{1} .$ The wire is then cut into two equal halves and a potential of~${V}_{0}$~is applied across the length of each half. The total power dissipation across two wires is~${P}_{2} .$ The ratio of~${P}_{2}: {P}_{1}$~is~$\sqrt{x}: 1 .$~The value of~$x$& is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the power dissipated in the first case can be written as

${P}_{1} = {V}_{0}^{2}R . . . \left(1\right)$

When the wire is halved, its resistance will also become half the previous value.

Thus, the formula to calculate the power dissipated in the second~case can be written as

\begin{cases}{P}_{2}$& = & ${V}_{0}^{2}\dfrac{R}{2} \times$2 \\ & = & $\dfrac{4{V0}^{2}}{R} . . . \left($2\right)\end{cases}$

Divide equation (2) by equation (1) to calculate the required ratio.

\begin{cases}\dfrac{P2}{P1}$& = & $\dfrac{4{V0}^{2}R}{{V0}^{2}R}$\\ & = & 4 \\ & = & $\sqrt{16}\end{cases}

Hence,~$x = 16.

$

questions.q: Two resistance of $100Ω$ and $200Ω$ are connected in series with a battery of $4V$ and negligible internal resistance. A voltmeter is used to measure voltage across $100Ω$ resistance, which gives reading as $1V$. The resistance of voltmeter must be _______ $Ω$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Voltage across $200Ω = 4 - 1 = 3V$.

Therefore, current through the battery, $\dfrac{3}{200}$

Now, equivalent resistance of ${R}_{V} & 100Ω$,$= \dfrac{{R}_{v}100}{{R}_{v} + 100}$

For voltmeter, $\dfrac{{R}_{v}100}{{R}_{v} + 100} \times \dfrac{3}{200} = 1$

$⇒ 3{R}_{v} = 2{R}_{v} + 200$

$⇒ {R}_{v} = 200Ω$

questions.q: Two wires of same length and thickness having specific resistances $6Ωcm$ and $3Ωcm$ respectively are connected in parallel. The effective resistivity is $ρΩcm$. The value of $ρ$ to the nearest integer, is ___ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$∵$ in parallel,~${R}_{net} = \dfrac{{R}_{1}{R}_{2}}{{R}_{1} + {R}_{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{ρl}{2A} = \dfrac{{ρ}_{1}\dfrac{l}{A} \times {ρ}_{2}\dfrac{l}{A}}{{ρ}_{1}\dfrac{l}{A} + {ρ}_{2}\dfrac{l}{A}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{ρ}{2} = \dfrac{6 \times 3}{6 + 3} = 2⇒ ρ = 4$

In the given circuit the value of& \left|\dfrac{{I}_{1} + {I}_{3}}{I2}\right|$ \text{ and } is:

questions.solution:
Potential distribution at each point in the circuit is shown in above diagram.

questions.q: The current density in a cylindrical wire of radius $4$ mm is $4 \times {10}^{6}Am^{- 2}$. The current through the outer portion of the wire between radial distances $\dfrac{R}{2}$ and $R$ is _____ $\piA$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Current density is defined as current per unit cross-section area. Therefore,

$i = JA = J \times \pi \left($R^{2} - $\dfrac{R2}{4}\right)

$⇒ i = 4 $\times {10}^{6} \times \pi \times$16 $\times {10}^{- 6} \times \dfrac{3}{4}

$⇒ i = 48\piA$

$

questions.q: In an electric circuit, a call of certain emf provides a potential difference of $1 . 25V$ across a load~resistance of $5Ω .$~However, it provides a potential difference of $1V$ across a load resistance of $2Ω .$The emf of the cell is given by $\dfrac{x}{10}V .$~Then the value of $x$ is .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Terminal voltage,& $v = iR = \dfrac{ER}{R + r}$

${1}^{st} \to 1 . 25 = \dfrac{E ( 5 )}{5 + r} \ldots \left(i\right)$
${2}^{nd} \to 1 = $\dfrac{E ( 2 )}{2 + r} \ldots \left(ii\right)$

By \left(i\right)\text{and} \left(ii\right)$,
$r = 1Ω, E = \dfrac{3}{2}V = \dfrac{15}{10}volt$
$⇒ x = 15

$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$P = i^{2}Rt$
$192 = 4 \times 4 \times R \times 1$
$R = 12Ω$
$P ' = \left(i '\right)2Rt$'
$= 8 \times 8 \times 12 \times 5 = 3840J$

questions.q: Two wires $A$ and $B$ are made up of the same material and have the same mass. Wire $A$ has radius of $2.0 \mathrm{~mm}$ and wire $B$ has radius of $4.0 \mathrm{~mm}$. The resistance of wire $B$ is $2 \Omega$. The resistance of wire $A$ is _____\Omega.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \because \mathrm{R}=\frac{\rho \ell}{\mathrm{A}}=\frac{\rho \mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{A}^2} \\ & \therefore \frac{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\frac{\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{B}}^2}{\mathrm{~A}_{\mathrm{A}}^2}=\frac{\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{B}}^4}{\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{A}}^4} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{A}}}{2}=\left[\frac{4 \times 10^{-3}}{2 \times 10^{-3}}\right]^4 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{A}}=32 \Omega .\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A network of four resistances is connected to $9V$ battery, as shown in figure. The magnitude of voltage difference between the points $A$ and $B$ is __________ $V$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The resistance in each branch is& $6Ω$. They are in parallel. So, net resistance is~$R ' = \dfrac{6}{2} = 3Ω$.

The total current flowing through the loop,

$I = \dfrac{V}{R '} = \dfrac{9V}{3Ω} = 3A$

Thus, through each branch the current is~$1 . 5A$.

Hence, the voltage difference across the points is

${V}_{A} - {V}_{B} = \left(4 \times 1 . 5\right) - \left(2 \times 1 . 5\right) = 3V$

questions.q: In the given figure of meter bridge experiment, the balancing length $AC$ corresponding to null deflection of the galvanometer is $40$ cm. The balancing length, if the radius of the wire $AB$ is doubled, will be _____ $cm$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: & Even if the radius of wire is doubled, the balancing point would not change as$\dfrac{x}{l - x} = \dfrac{R1}{R2}$ , which is independent of area in case of uniform wire. Thus, the balancing length remains the same i.e.,~$40$ cm.

questions.q: The current density in a cylindrical wire of radius $r = 4 . 0mm$ is $1 . 0 \times {10}^{6}A^{2}m^{2}$. The current through the outer portion of the wire between radial distances $\dfrac{r}{2}$ and $r$ is $x\piA$; where $x$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Current $= J \times$ Area

$= J \times \pi\left[R^{2} - \left(\dfrac{R}{2}\right)\right]2 = J\pi\dfrac{3R^{2}}{4} = {10}^{6} \times \pi \times 3 \times \left(\dfrac{4 \times {10}^{- 3}}{4}\right)2$

$⇒ \pi \times 3 \times \dfrac{16}{4} = 12\piA$

Hence, the value of~$x = 12$.

questions.q: A steel rod with $y = 2 . 0 \times {10}^{11}Nm^{- 2}$ and $\alpha = {10}^{- 5}{C ∘}^{- 1}$ of length $4m$ and area of cross-section $10{cm}^{2}$ is heated from $0 ° C$ to $400 ° C$ without being allowed to extend. The tension produced in the rod is $x \times {10}^{5}N$ where the value of $x$ is~_________ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Thermal force $F = Ay\alpha\Delta T$

$F = \left(10 \times {10}^{- 4}\right) \times \left(2 \times {10}^{11}\right)\left({10}^{- 5}\right) ( 400 )$
$F = 8 \times {10}^{5}N$
$⇒ x = 8$

questions.q: If the potential difference between $B$ and $D$ is zero, the value of $x$ is~$\dfrac{1}{n}Ω$.~The value of $n$ is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As potential difference between B & D is zero therefore it is& a balanced& wheatstone bridge. So, we can write

$⇒ \dfrac{R1}{R2} = \dfrac{R3}{R4} ⇒ \left(\dfrac{6 \times 3}{6 + 3}\right)1 + 2 = \left(\dfrac{x \times 1}{x + 1}\right)x$

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{1}{x + 1}$

$⇒ x = 0 . 5 = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Hence, required~$n = 2$.
